# Direct democracy (citizen assembly voting on laws) (`citizen_assembly`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/institutions.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Institutions, law & governance (`institutions`)
- Deps: helped by sortition, secret_ballot
- Core idea: The assembled citizens vote on laws themselves, in person, instead of choosing representatives to do it for them. Athens ran a city of some 30,000 citizens this way for nearly two centuries, alongside offices filled by lot.
- Pitfalls:
  - Idealising Athens: women, slaves and resident foreigners, the large majority, had no part
  - Assuming it scales: a face-to-face assembly works for a city, not a kingdom
- History: greece: 508/507 BC – Cleisthenes' reforms at Athens: assembly of all citizens and a council of 500; direct, not representative
- Read:
  - Mogens Herman Hansen, The Athenian Democracy in the Age of Demosthenes (1991)
  - Aristotle, Athenaion Politeia (Constitution of the Athenians), c. 330 BC
